rules.rule:
Tests are the guard (this repository uses both `.test.ts` and `.spec.ts`), so a test that cannot fail is the worst defect in the change.

- Flag a test asserting a value it also computed.
- Flag a mock so permissive that the assertion holds regardless of the code under test.
- Flag a test that depends on ambient environment (a real `.env`, a live network, the clock)
  where an injected value was available — an environment-dependent test passes on the author's
  machine and proves nothing in CI.
- Flag a queue-style fake that runs out of responses mid-test: once it returns a default, the
  remaining assertions describe the fake, not the code.

Repositories, where a missing filter becomes a data leak.

## Every query is scoped to the workspace

Rows in this schema carry `workspace_id`, and roughly nine hundred repository call sites pass a
workspace through. A query that omits it returns another customer's data and looks perfectly
correct in a test with one workspace in the database.

- Flag ANY new query, count, aggregate or `EXISTS` that does not constrain the workspace, and say
  plainly that this is a cross-tenant leak rather than a style issue.
- Flag an update or delete located by id alone where the table is workspace-scoped: an id from
  one workspace must not be actionable from another.
- Flag a soft-deleted row included where the rest of the module filters `deleted_at IS NULL`, and
  the reverse. A partial unique index means a key can be reused after a soft delete, so the two
  must agree or uniqueness differs between code and database.

## Performance
- Flag a query inside a loop over rows just fetched — that is the N+1 shape.
- Flag a list endpoint with no limit.

HTTP controllers.

## Authorization is explicit on every route

Twenty-four controllers here declare permissions with `@RequirePermission`. A new route without
one is open to any authenticated caller, and nothing in a test will say so.

- Flag a new route with no permission declaration, and name the permission its neighbours use.
- Where a permission is scoped to a resource read from the request, check the request actually
  carries that field. A guard reading `projectId` from the query fails with a permission error
  when the parameter is simply absent, which sends the reader to look for missing access instead
  of a missing parameter.
- Flag a route that takes an id and does not verify the caller may see that id.

## Contract
- A response shape is a contract. Flag a removed or renamed field, a narrowed type, or a changed
  status code without a note on who consumes it.
- Flag a new required request field on an existing route; existing callers become invalid.

Request and response DTOs are the API's contract, and a generated client is derived from them.

- A change here changes the OpenAPI document, so the committed generated client must be
  regenerated in the same pull request. It is a 437 KB file produced from a running server, and
  forgetting it fails the contract check with a diff rather than a clear message.
- Flag a field added to a DTO that is not also carried through the service and the repository. A
  field validated and then dropped before the row is the hardest kind of bug to see: the request
  succeeds.
- Flag a validation rule loosened without a reason, and a regex or length limit that disagrees
  with the database column.

Background work. Delivery here is at-least-once, so a handler will run twice.

- Flag a handler whose effect is not idempotent — sending mail, charging, incrementing — with no
  key or guard that makes a repeat harmless.
- Flag a job with no retry policy, and a retry with no backoff.
- Flag a failure path that swallows the error: a job that fails silently is worse than one that
  is retried loudly.
- Flag unbounded work in one job where the input grows; batch it.

Outbound calls.

- Every request needs a timeout and an explicit failure path.
- A write must send `Content-Type`; at least one provider rejects a body without it and the
  error names the body, not the header.
- Paginated endpoints differ: some take a page number, some a cursor. Sending the wrong one is
  accepted and silently returns the first page forever.
- Flag a response parsed without checking status.

QNSC TypeScript conventions, on top of the built-in TypeScript rules.

## Layering

The backend services follow ports-and-adapters: `interface/` (HTTP, DTOs) -> `application/`
(services) -> `domain/` (types, ports) -> `infrastructure/` (repositories). A dependency
pointing the wrong way is the defect that makes a module impossible to test.

- Flag a `domain/` file importing from `infrastructure/` or `interface/`.
- Flag HTTP concerns (request objects, status codes, headers) appearing in `application/`.
- Flag SQL or an ORM call outside `infrastructure/`.

## A repository that whitelists columns must include the new one

Update methods here list every column they set. A field added to a DTO and to the domain type
but not to that list is accepted by the API, validated, and silently discarded. This has
happened: a key could be sent, passed validation, and never reach the row.

- When a pull request adds a field to an update path, verify it is present in EVERY layer
  between the schema and the row, and name the layer that is missing.

## Optionality must be read through the helper, not guessed from the field list

Fields are often built by named helpers whose suffix carries the optionality. Judging a field
required because the schema line looks required produces false findings.

- Before reporting a field as required or optional, follow the helper it is built from.

## Errors

- An error message must say what the caller should do differently. `PERMISSION_DENIED` on a
  request whose real fault was a missing query parameter sends the reader to the wrong place.
- Flag a thrown error whose message names neither the offending value nor the remedy.
- Flag a caught error that is swallowed without logging or rethrowing.

## Tests

- A new branch needs a test that fails without it.
- Prefer asserting on observable behaviour over internal calls, except where the defect being
  guarded is precisely that a call was missing.

## Logging
- Nothing personal or secret in a log line: no tokens, no email addresses, no request body
  that might carry either.
- A new external call needs a log or span on failure; an unattributable timeout is the
  hardest thing to diagnose.
